title: Plugin scope ruling 28: managed decides over every scope and a managed deciding row is never updated
description: Binding record: opum-doc main 7818aca8b, docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md, Amendment 6 (ODOC-286, commit 44326c508, opum-ai/opum-doc#458), ruling 28. Read it there before implementing. The full scope order is managed > local > project > user > synced. This supersedes ruling 26(ii) for managed only: managed decides ahead of the rest when present and applicable (Claude Code's own code treats a managed row as applicable to every project, as it does user). A managed deciding row is NEVER updated: no '--scope managed' update runs (Claude Code itself refuses with 'Cannot install plugins to managed scope'); state is reported with scope 'managed', and the remedy names the administrator's managed settings in prose, not a command the user can run. lore-cli owes this because dc09ca98 (LCLI-592, opum-ai/lore-cli#291) implements ruling 26's order. Per the orchestrator's 2026-09-26 agreement, this task owns everything managed: the detection precedence in src/core/agent-plugins.ts / src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts AND the update guard in LCLI-593's --target --force update path. Ruling 29 (the deepest-projectPath tie-break within one scope) is already implemented by dc09ca98 and is now binding; keep it. A managed row's real rendering is unmeasured on any install (Amendment 6 provenance), so tests use recorded outputs built from the schema Amendment 6 measured.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Detection orders scopes managed > local > project > user > synced, so an applicable managed row decides over every other scope (including a project-matching local row), proven by tests over recorded list outputs with managed enabled and managed disabled

A managed deciding row is never updated: lore agents --target claude --force runs no update against it, reports scope managed with update not-run, and its remedy is prose naming the administrator managed settings, not a runnable command; proven through a stub runtime that logs every call
Ruling 29 (deepest projectPath within one scope) still holds, and docs (cli-surface, cli-contract, lore instructions agents) state the order; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0
